title: FOMC Press Conference, September 16, 2026
summary: Fed chair Warsh explains a quarter-point hike: inflation above target for five years, price rises broad across categories, labor market at full employment, and the Fed can stop an energy shock from spreading.

assertions.quote: for more than five years, inflation has been running above target

verdicts.note: PCE inflation has exceeded 2% every month since early 2021.

The 12-month CPI-U change has been at least 2.3% in every month from March 2021 (2.6%) through September 2026 (3.7%), five and a half years; the Fed's target is on PCE inflation, which runs somewhat below CPI, so the lowest CPI readings (2.3% in April 2025) leave a small margin.

assertions.quote: Too many categories are still posting increases above 3 percent on both a 6- and 12-month basis.
This summer's inflation readings do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved.

verdicts.note: Core PCE held near 3.2% and the three-month core run rate rose from about 2% to 3.4% by September.

Core CPI 12-month growth fell from 2.8% in May 2026 to 2.6% in June, 2.5% in July and 2.4% in August before ticking back to 2.6% in September, and the June-August seasonally adjusted monthly readings (-0.0%, 0.2%, 0.3%) annualize to about 2%, so underlying inflation did improve over the summer before the September rebound.

assertions.quote: We cannot affect any individual price, whether it be oil prices

verdicts.note: Standard central-bank doctrine: rates act on demand and expectations, not oil supply, and second-round effects are what policy targets.

assertions.quote: the unemployment rate is basically running consistent with full employment

verdicts.note: Unemployment near 4.1% with jobless claims at full-employment levels matches most estimates of the natural rate.

Unemployment was 4.2% in September 2026 and has stayed in a 4.1-4.3% range since March, near common estimates of the natural rate, but payroll growth was weak (+29,000, 45,000/month average) and the release does not define full employment.

assertions.quote: the least well off are the ones who have the most to gain from stable prices

verdicts.note: Paycheck-to-paycheck households cannot offset price rises with asset gains and spend more of their income on energy and food.

assertions.quote: First is economic strength. Part of the reason why we've seen, over the course of 2026, long-term yields go up is, the economy has strengthened.
most advanced economies are facing price pressures

verdicts.note: The 2026 oil shock hit every importer and the ECB also hiked twice, though US tariffs are a US-specific source.

assertions.quote: I don't believe that we need to do harm to the labor markets to achieve our objective.

verdicts.note: A forecast; the 2022-24 disinflation happened without recession, but tightening into a supply shock has often cost jobs.
